correctness.rationale: For finite connected simple graph n>=2 with no triangles/four-cycles, the directed graph uses BOTH orientations of every edge and the nonregular cubic Mayer differential ∂(v0,...,vk)=sum ξ^j delete_j, with ξ a primitive cube root. Distinguish allowed words and unallowed repeated-coordinate faces. Ω0=CV and Ω1=C^(oriented edges); opposite arc boundary columns give rank ∂1=n. A length-two walk with distinct endpoints has a uniquely inadmissible middle deletion by girth>=5, so Ω2 contains only backtracks with local coefficients summing to zero, giving dim Ω2=2m-n. In degree three successive unique forbidden faces force every walk coefficient zero, hence Ω3=0. On the backtrack balance lattice, ∂ is injective by invertible opposite-arc 2x2 blocks, whereas ∂²b_vw=e_v-e_w and its image is the span of equal-neighbor vertex differences, rank n-c(G), c=2 for bipartite and 1 otherwise. The two distinct q-homologies are therefore β^(3,1)=(c,2m-n,0,0), β^(3,2)=(0,n,2m-2n+c,0); the equivariant port exact sequence gives automorphism trace formulas f_evenclass, f_arcs-f_vertices, f_vertices, f_arcs-2f_vertices+f_evenclass. Finite-field independent construction verifies representative cases but the graph-general forbidden-face proof supplies universality.
